analyst_observations: The key discriminating assertions are review-checklist (with-skill always produces a §11 checklist table; baseline never does) and review-uses-severity-groups (with-skill uses strict HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW; baseline free-forms severity labels).

The findings-identify-networkidle assertion failed for BOTH configurations — because the reviewed files (cart.spec.ts, cart.page.ts) genuinely don't contain networkidle. This assertion is non-discriminating and should be removed or rewritten to test whether the reviewer examines BasePage as context.

Eval 2 (review-only) shows equal scores (5/6) for both configurations — suggesting that for pure review tasks without standards generation, the skill adds less marginal value. The main win is consistent structure (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW labels and file:line format).
The biggest win is Eval 0 (6/6 vs 4/6): the skill enforces the combined generate+review workflow with cross-referencing, which the baseline doesn't do unprompted.

The baseline's Eval 1 output had 17 sections (more comprehensive in breadth) but lacked a review checklist. The skill-guided output had 11 sections + an appendix but always produced the checklist — a clearer deliverable for a code reviewer.
